summary:
Earth Jukebox is an interactive Earth science platform that transforms real environmental data into sound, offering an alternative way to explore and understand our planet. By combining scientific data sonification with interactive visualizations, the project makes complex environmental measurements more engaging and accessible.

Users can select any geographical location and explore atmospheric parameters such as temperature, rainfall, wind speed and surface temperature using NASA POWER data. Through the Web Audio API, these measurements are translated into distinct sound patterns. The platform further integrates NASA MODIS NDVI imagery for vegetation monitoring, NOAA satellite data for ocean temperature and chlorophyll-a, and historical climate comparisons to explore environmental changes across different years.

By connecting data, visualization and sound, Earth Jukebox aims to transform the way people experience Earth science, encouraging environmental awareness, scientific curiosity and inclusive exploration of our changing planet.
details:
Project Details – Earth Jukebox

1. Project Overview

Earth Jukebox is an interactive Earth-science platform that transforms real environmental measurements into sound. It combines data sonification, interactive maps and scientific visualizations to provide an alternative way of exploring Earth's changing environmental systems.

Users can select geographical locations, retrieve environmental data and experience the measurements through both visual and auditory representations.

2. How It Works

The platform retrieves daily environmental measurements from NASA POWER, including:

  • Air temperature at 2 metres (T2M).
  • Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR).
  • Wind speed at 10 metres (WS10M).
  • Earth skin temperature (TS).

The retrieved measurements are validated and mapped to audio parameters using the Web Audio API.

Each variable has a distinct sound representation. Temperature controls musical pitch, rainfall controls the frequency of short sound pulses, wind influences noise brightness and loudness, and surface temperature produces a slow, wave-like tone.

Users can also listen to a sequence representing the last 30 days of measurements and explore how environmental conditions change over time.

3. Additional Features

Beyond atmospheric data, Earth Jukebox incorporates three additional exploration modules:

Vegetation Monitoring: NASA MODIS NDVI imagery, accessed through NASA GIBS, allows users to explore vegetation greenness across different years.

Ocean Monitoring: NOAA CoastWatch satellite products provide sea-surface temperature and chlorophyll-a measurements where data is available.

Historical Climate Comparison: Users can compare monthly temperature, precipitation and wind patterns between two selected years through interactive charts and audio sequences.

4. Technologies Used

The application is developed using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript. Its primary technologies and resources include:

  • NASA POWER API – Environmental measurements.
  • NASA GIBS and MODIS – Vegetation imagery.
  • NOAA CoastWatch ERDDAP – Ocean measurements.
  • Leaflet.js and OpenStreetMap – Interactive maps.
  • Web Audio API – Real-time sound generation.
  • HTML Canvas – Data visualization.
  • Browser Geolocation API – Location selection.

The platform runs directly in a web browser without requiring additional software installation.

5. Innovation and Impact

The central innovation of Earth Jukebox is its use of sound as an additional medium for communicating scientific data. Instead of relying exclusively on conventional charts, maps and numerical readings, it translates environmental measurements into distinct auditory patterns.

This approach has potential applications in environmental education, public science communication and accessible exploration of Earth science.

By connecting real environmental data with sound and interactive visualization, Earth Jukebox aims to make complex planetary information more engaging, understandable and accessible.
